review_text: Located right in the heart of HSR Layout, this Indian Coffee House has a large and well-arranged dining area with a classic old-style charm. The service was polite and friendly, though it may take a little time for food to reach the table, especially during busy hours. This outlet follows the same legacy and vibe as the Indian Coffee House branches we see in Kerala, though this particular chain originally started in Jabalpur and has now grown to around 22 outlets.We had ghee roast, Masala Dosa and Vada Sambar. The ghee roast was for kid, but it was so hard.  There is also a hall on the fifth floor which can be used for gatherings or meetings, which is a nice bonus. Parking is available in the underground area, which is definitely helpful in this busy locality.  Food quality is good and comforting, though I felt the pricing was slightly on the higher side considering the overall traditional menu. Still, it is a nice place to sit, relax, and enjoy a calm meal.

review_text: Overpriced and Absolutely Not Worth It  One of the most unpleasant experiences I’ve had. The watchman stands at the entrance constantly asking customers for tips, which is annoying right from the start and again at the exit. Inside, the staff is rude, judgy, unprofessional, and refuses to take any feedback.  The huge menu is pointless — nothing is made properly and the food is wildly inconsistent every single time. The so-called fruit sundaes taste artificial, the French toast is terrible, and even the coffee is below basic standards — ironic for a place called Indian Coffee House, tough competition for another place called “The Filter Coffee” claiming to be the best for coffee which is again another worst place.  Tables are never clean, service is slow, and there’s clear favoritism in how they treat certain customers.  For all this, the place is extremely expensive, making the experience even worse. Underwhelming, unpleasant, and absolutely not recommended.

review_text: While I was taking my weekend strolls in HSR, I came across this multi-cuisine restaurant run by Indian coffee workers co operative society ltd Jabalpur,  Even though I wasn’t much hungry just thought of giving it a try.  The ambiance of the restaurant is quite classy and looks sophisticated with the clean and tidy atmosphere. The entire restaurant is air conditioned, which makes it a perfect place for hot summers.  Since restaurant wasn’t crowded I chose one of the big tables to dine in and relax. After going through the entire menu, I settled down for my all time favourite masala dosa and to a glass of fresh orange juice for the hot weather.  While my order was being prepared, I explored the restaurant, it has got a clean n tidy hand wash area, a beautiful aquarium with lots of tiny fish and a lobby to enter their party hall.  When I received my order, I was awestruck with the size of the masala dosa, it was literally size of a paper dosa, so I just double confirmed with the waiter if the order was right.!  The dosa did look good but could have tasted better, the chatney was delicious and sambar complimented the chatney instead complimenting the dosa. Since it was huge it got dry n cold by the time I finished just half of it. A spoon of oil or ghee could have saved the dish.  Orange juice was really made from real fruits, I got to know it instantly because they had forgotten to remove the seeds, which did add a bitter note to the drink. But I was quite happy because they hadn’t added any artificial colors or artificial sweeteners.  Overall it’s a reasonable and decent place in HSR for your meals, either with friends or family, it just fits good.  PS: I wanted to rate 5, but deducting one star for the seeds in the orange juice and half a star for masala dosa. So actual rating is 3.5
